t: In cockroach wings are absent in
s: In cockroach, the thorax has three segments. The mesothorax bears the forewings (tegmina) and the metathorax bears the hind wings, while the prothorax bears no wings. Each thoracic segment, however, bears a pair of walking legs.

t: Number of salivary glands present in cockroach is
s: Cockroach has a single pair of salivary glands lying near the crop. Each gland has a salivary reservoir, and their ducts open via a common salivary duct at the base of the hypopharynx. Saliva helps in moistening and digesting food.

t: In cockroach, digestive juice is secreted by
s: Hepatic (gastric) caecae, 6–8 blind tubules at the junction of foregut and midgut, secrete digestive juice. The oesophagus is a conducting tube, the crop stores food and the gizzard (proventriculus) grinds food with chitinous teeth; none of these secretes digestive enzymes.

t: The number of abdominal segments in male and female cockroach is
s: The abdomen of cockroach consists of 10 segments in both males and females. In females the 7th sternum is boat shaped and with the 8th and 9th sterna forms the genital pouch, while males have the genital pouch at the hind end, but the segment number remains 10 in both.

t: Number of chambers present in the heart of cockroach is
s: The heart of cockroach is an elongated muscular tube lying along the mid dorsal line of thorax and abdomen. It is differentiated into 13 funnel shaped chambers with ostia on either side, through which haemolymph enters from the sinuses.

t: Select the correct option regarding Rana tigrina-
s: Rana tigrina (Indian bullfrog) adults are carnivores feeding on insects, worms and other small animals caught with a bilobed protrusible tongue. They are not omnivores (tadpoles feed on plants), development is indirect through a tadpole larva, and frogs have both hepatic portal and renal portal systems, not hepatic portal only.

t: Which of the following gland is absent in frog?
s: Frog has a liver (largest gland), a pancreas, and endocrine glands including the pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal and adrenals. Salivary glands are absent; food is lubricated by mucus from buccal glands. Hence salivary gland is the absent gland.

t: Bidder's Canal in frog
s: In male frog, vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidney and open into Bidder's canal, which runs inside the kidney and communicates with the urinogenital duct (ureter) that opens into the cloaca. Thus it carries sperm from the kidney to the urinogenital duct, not from testis or carrying urine.

Carries urine from kidney to ureter

t: In female cockroaches, sperms are stored in which part of the reproductive system?
s: In female cockroach, a pair of spermathecae, present in the 6th abdominal segment, opens into the genital chamber and stores sperms received during copulation. Seminal vesicles and mushroom glands belong to the male system, while collaterial glands secrete the ootheca material.

t: Bundles of sperms in cockroach are called
s: In male cockroach, sperms stored in the seminal vesicles are glued together into bundles called spermatophores, which are discharged during copulation. Spermathecae store sperms in the female, seminal plasma is fluid part of semen, and gonophore is the male genital opening.

t: The function of the gap junction is to
s: Gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, facilitating communication by rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules. Cementing neighbouring cells together is done by adhering junctions, and preventing leakage of substances across a tissue is the role of tight junctions.

t: Tendon is an example of which of the following connective tissue?
s: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones and are dense regular connective tissue, in which collagen fibres are arranged in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, giving tensile strength. Loose connective tissue has loosely arranged cells and fibres, while specialised connective tissues include cartilage, bone and blood.

t: Fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells are present in the
s: Fibroblasts (secrete fibres), macrophages (phagocytic) and mast cells (secrete histamine, heparin) are characteristic cells of connective tissue, especially areolar tissue, along with collagen and elastic fibres in a ground substance. Epithelium and muscle tissues have no such cells or abundant matrix.

t:

s: Squamous epithelium lines blood vessels (a-4), cuboidal epithelium occurs in ducts of glands and tubular parts of kidney nephrons (b-3), columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestine (c-1), and ciliated epithelium lines the fallopian tubes and bronchioles to move particles or ova (d-2).

t: Collagen fibres are secreted by
s: Fibroblasts are the most abundant cells of connective tissue and secrete collagen and elastic fibres as well as the ground substance (modified polysaccharides). Mast cells secrete histamine and heparin, macrophages are phagocytic, and osteocytes are bone cells lying in lacunae.

t: Identify the specialised connective tissue in which it's intercellular material is solid and pliable and resists compression
s: Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue whose intercellular material is solid, pliable and resists compression; chondrocytes lie in lacunae within it. Bone has a hard, non-pliable matrix rich in calcium salts, blood has a fluid matrix, and muscle is not a connective tissue.

b) A tissue is a group of similar cells along with intercellular substances and perform a specific function
c) Tissues are organised in specific proportion to form organs

Of the above statements
s: All are correct. Animal tissues are classified by structure and function into four types: epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. t: Dense irregular connective tissue is present in
s: Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres, mostly collagen, oriented differently, and is present in the skin (dermis). Tendons and ligaments are dense regular tissues with parallel collagen fibres, while cartilage is a specialised connective tissue.

t: 'Anal cerci' found in cockroach are helpful in
s: Anal cerci are a pair of jointed filamentous structures on the 10th abdominal segment of both sexes. They are sensory, bearing hairs that detect sound and air vibrations, helping the cockroach sense approaching danger. Locomotion uses legs, and odour production is by stink glands.

s: Statement C is wrong: the cartilage matrix contains chondrocytes enclosed in small cavities (lacunae) in a solid, pliable chondroitin matrix, not mast cells and macrophages, which are features of areolar tissue. Adipose tissue stores fats, ligaments connect bone to bone and tendons attach skeletal muscle to bone.

t: The type of epithelium found on the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs forming a diffusion boundary is known as
s: Simple squamous epithelium is a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. It is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs (alveoli) of lungs, and its thinness allows rapid diffusion, making it a diffusion boundary. Cuboidal, columnar and pseudostratified epithelia are too thick for this role.

t: The cuboidal epithelium is composed of a single layer of cube like cells, which help in secretion and absorption are located in
s: Cuboidal epithelium is a single layer of cube-like cells found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys, where it functions in secretion and absorption; in PCT it bears microvilli. Stomach and intestine have columnar, bronchioles and fallopian tubes ciliated, and trachea pseudostratified ciliated epithelium.

t: Goblet cells are example for
s: Goblet cells are isolated mucus-secreting columnar cells in the alimentary canal and respiratory tract, and are examples of unicellular glands. Multicellular glands are clusters of cells such as salivary glands; endocrine glands are ductless and heterocrine glands like pancreas have both exocrine and endocrine parts.

s: Statement A is incorrect: in nearly all animal tissues, specialised junctions provide structural and functional links between cells; they are not restricted to epithelium (e.g. intercalated discs in cardiac muscle). Tight, adhering and gap junctions are its types; gap junctions transfer ions and molecules, and tight junctions prevent leakage across a tissue.

- It contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.
The above description is based on:
s: Areolar tissue, a loose connective tissue present beneath the skin, often serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells with collagen and elastic fibres. Adipose tissue is specialised to store fat, while tendons and ligaments are dense regular tissues with few cells.

t: The upper lip in the mouth parts of cockroach is:
s: The mouth parts of cockroach include labrum (upper lip), a pair of mandibles, a pair of maxillae and labium (lower lip). The median flexible lobe hypopharynx acts as a tongue within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts. Hence the upper lip is the labrum.

t: The first pair of wings of cockroach arises from:
s: The first pair of wings, the forewings or tegmina, are dark, opaque and leathery and arise from the mesothorax, covering the hind wings at rest. The second pair (membranous hind wings used in flight) arises from the metathorax. The prothorax and abdomen bear no wings.

t: Which is wrong regarding proventriculus of cockroach?
s: Statement A is wrong: food is stored in the crop, not the proventriculus. The proventriculus (gizzard) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth, which grind the food particles.
o: It is used for storing of food.

Six highly chitinous plates called teeth are present in proventriculus.

t: The ring of 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous structures present at the junction of mid gut and hind gut are:
s: At the junction of midgut and hindgut of cockroach lies a ring of 100–150 yellow coloured thin filamentous Malpighian tubules. They remove nitrogenous wastes from haemolymph as uric acid. Hepatic (gastric) caecae, 6–8 in number, lie at the junction of foregut and midgut.

t: The number of spiracles present in cockroach are:
s: The respiratory system of cockroach consists of a network of tracheae that open to the outside through 10 pairs of small spiracles on the lateral side of the body: 2 pairs in the thorax and 8 pairs in the abdomen. Their opening is regulated by sphincters.

s: Statement A is wrong: each compound eye (not both together) consists of about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia. Each ommatidium receives a part of the image, so the cockroach receives several images of an object; this mosaic vision gives more sensitivity but less resolution, mainly at night. So B, C and D are correct.

t: Hind gut of cockroach is differentiated into:
s: The alimentary canal of cockroach has foregut, midgut and hindgut. The hindgut is broader than the midgut and is differentiated into ileum, colon and rectum, the rectum opening out through the anus. Oesophagus, crop and gizzard belong to the foregut, and duodenum, jejunum and ileum are parts of the human small intestine.

t: Body of a adult frog is divisible into:
s: The body of an adult frog is divisible into head and trunk only. A neck and tail are absent (the tail is present only in the tadpole larva). Head, middle piece and tail describe a sperm, not a frog.

t: Which of the following is/are absent in female frog?
s: Frogs show sexual dimorphism: male frogs have sound producing vocal sacs and a copulatory (nuptial) pad on the first digit of the forelimbs, both absent in females. The tympanum (eardrum), which receives sound signals, is present in both sexes. Hence both 2 and 3 are absent in females.

t: The ureters act as urinogenital duct which opens into the cloaca. This is applicable to:
s: In male frog, sperms from the testes pass through vasa efferentia and Bidder's canal into the ureter, so the ureter carries both urine and sperms and acts as a urinogenital duct opening into the cloaca. In females the ureters carry only urine, while ova pass through separate oviducts.
o: Neither male frog nor the female frog

t: Haemolymph of cockroach contains:
s: The haemolymph of cockroach is colourless and is composed of plasma and haemocytes. It lacks erythrocytes and respiratory pigment such as haemoglobin, because gaseous exchange occurs directly through tracheae. Hence haemocytes and plasma.

s: In the head of cockroach, the brain is represented by the supra-oesophageal ganglion, which supplies nerves to the antennae and compound eyes. t:
Cardiac muscles are:
I) striated
II) voluntary
III) involuntary
IV) non-striated
s: Cardiac muscle fibres are branched and striated (showing light and dark bands like skeletal muscle) but are involuntary, contracting rhythmically without conscious control. They are not voluntary like skeletal muscle and not non-striated like smooth muscle. Hence I and III.

t: In Periplaneta, digestive juice is secreted by:
s: In Periplaneta (cockroach), a ring of 6–8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caecae at the junction of foregut and midgut secretes digestive juice. Malpighian tubules are excretory, the gizzard grinds food with chitinous teeth, and the crop stores food.

t: Cloacal aperture of male frog is used to pass out:
s: In male frog the cloaca is a common chamber receiving the rectum (faeces), and the urinogenital ducts (ureters) that carry both urine and sperms. All of these pass to the exterior through the single cloacal aperture. Hence faeces, urine and sperms are all passed out through it.

t: The epithelium of PCT of nephron in kidney has:
s: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron is lined by cuboidal epithelium whose free surface bears microvilli, forming a brush border that increases surface area for reabsorption. Irregular boundaries are a feature of squamous epithelium, slender cells of columnar epithelium, and cilia of ciliated epithelium.

t: Which of the following is not applicable to Rana?
s: Adult Rana is ureotelic, excreting urea, not uric acid; uricotelism is seen in birds, reptiles and insects. Frogs do have a three chambered heart (two atria, one ventricle), use lungs for breathing on land, and show external fertilisation in water.

t: The location of Nuptial pad in male frog:
s: During the breeding season, male frogs develop a copulatory or nuptial pad on the first digit of each forelimb. It helps the male clasp the female firmly during amplexus. It is absent in females and is not present on all digits, the hindlimb toes or in the buccal cavity.

t: During hibernation frog shows:
s: During hibernation (and aestivation) the frog remains inactive in mud or burrows, and its low oxygen requirement is met entirely through the moist, highly vascular skin, i.e. cutaneous respiration. Pulmonary (lung) respiration is used on land when active, and branchial (gill) respiration occurs only in tadpoles.

The other statements are correct: tegmina arise from the mesothorax, anal cerci occur in both sexes on the 10th segment, and anal styles are present only in males.

The nymph grows by moulting about 2 times to reach the adult form

t: Which of these structures in frog receive sound signals?
s: The tympanum (eardrum), a membranous structure on either side of the head behind the eyes, receives sound signals. Webbed feet help in swimming, the skin is for respiration and water absorption, and the nictitating membrane protects the eyes underwater.

t: Cells that support and protect neurons are:
s: Neuroglia (glial cells) make up more than half the volume of neural tissue; they support and protect neurons and do not conduct impulses. Nerve cells (neurons) are the excitable units, Sertoli cells nourish sperms in the testis, and protein filaments are not cells.

t: Chitinous asymmetrical structures present in Periplaneta, which surrounds the male gonopore is:
s: In male cockroach, the external genitalia are represented by male gonapophyses or phallomeres, which are chitinous asymmetrical structures surrounding the male gonopore. Collaterial glands and vestibulum belong to the female system, and caudal (anal) styles are slender appendages on the 9th sternum of males.

t: Bidder's canal is associated with:
s: Bidder's canal is part of the male reproductive system of frog. Vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidneys and open into Bidder's canal, which communicates with the urinogenital duct opening into the cloaca. Cockroaches and female frogs lack it.

t: What type of respiration is shown by frogs in water?
s: In water, a frog respires through its moist, thin and highly vascular skin by diffusion, i.e. cutaneous respiration. Pulmonary respiration through lungs and buccal respiration occur on land, while branchial (gill) respiration is seen only in tadpole larvae.

t: Which of these is not present in frog?
s: Frog erythrocytes are oval, biconvex and nucleated, so non-nucleated erythrocytes are not present (non-nucleated RBCs are characteristic of mammals). Frogs do have a hepatic portal system, a renal portal system and a lymphatic system.

t: Which one of the following characteristics is common to both in humans and adult frogs?
s: Both humans and adult frogs are ureotelic, excreting nitrogenous waste mainly as urea. Frogs have a three chambered heart (humans four), external fertilisation (humans internal) and nucleated RBCs (human RBCs lack nuclei), so the other options are not common to both.

t: In a female cockroach brood pouch or genital pouch is formed by:
s: In female cockroach, the 7th sternum is boat shaped, and together with the 8th and 9th sterna forms a brood or genital pouch, whose anterior part contains the female gonopore, spermathecal pores and collaterial glands. Terga are dorsal plates and pleura lateral membranes, which do not form it.

t: The connective tissue which connects muscle to bone is:
s: Tendons are dense regular connective tissue that attach skeletal muscles to bones. Ligaments connect bone to bone, cartilage is a specialised connective tissue found at joints, nose tip and ear, and areolar tissue is loose connective tissue beneath the skin.

t: Intercalated disc is present in which of the following type of muscle?
s: Intercalated discs are communication junctions where plasma membranes of adjacent cardiac muscle cells fuse, allowing the cells to contract as a unit. They are absent in skeletal muscle (long multinucleate fibres) and smooth muscle (fusiform cells joined by ordinary cell junctions).

t: Dense irregular connective tissue present in
s: Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) oriented differently, and is present in the skin (dermis). Tendons and ligaments are dense regular tissues with parallel collagen bundles, and areolar tissue is loose connective tissue.

t: The connective tissue present in the tip of nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent bones of the vertebral column, limbs and hands in adults is:
s: Cartilage, with a solid, pliable matrix resisting compression, is present in the tip of nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent bones of the vertebral column, and in limbs and hands in adults. Bone is hard and non-pliable, tendons join muscle to bone, and areolar tissue lies beneath skin.

t: The epithelial tissue found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs and are involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary is:
s: Squamous epithelium is a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. It forms the walls of blood vessels and air sacs (alveoli) of lungs, where it acts as a diffusion boundary. Cuboidal epithelium lines ducts and nephron tubules, columnar lines stomach and intestine, and ciliated lines bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

t: The grinding regions and incising regions are present in which type of mouth parts of cockroach?
s: Each mandible of cockroach is a hard, chitinous jaw bearing incisor (incising) regions with teeth for cutting food and molar (grinding) regions for crushing it. The labrum is the upper lip, maxillae help hold and manipulate food, and the gizzard is a part of the gut, not a mouth part.

t: A ring of 6-8 blind tubules, present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice in cockroach is:
s: At the junction of foregut and midgut in cockroach lies a ring of 6–8 blind tubules secreting digestive juice. They are called hepatic caecae or gastric caecae, both names referring to the same structures. Malpighian tubules (100–150) at the midgut–hindgut junction are excretory.

t: The body of cockroach is divided into:
s: The body of cockroach is segmented and divisible into three distinct regions: head, thorax and abdomen, the entire body being covered by a hard chitinous exoskeleton. There is no tail, and the head and thorax are not fused into a cephalothorax as in prawns and spiders.

t: The head of cockroach is formed by the fusion of:
s: The head of cockroach is triangular and is formed by the fusion of six segments. It shows great mobility in all directions due to a flexible neck. It bears a pair of compound eyes, a pair of antennae and the mouth parts.

t: Spiracles in cockroach are located in:
s: Cockroach respires through tracheae that open to the outside by 10 pairs of spiracles on the lateral side of the body: 2 pairs on the thorax and 8 pairs on the abdomen. There are no spiracles on the head.

t: Which statement is correct regarding female cockroach?
s: Both male and female cockroaches have 10 abdominal segments. Anal styles are present only in males, not females, while anal cerci are present in both sexes on the 10th segment. Hence the correct statement for females is abdomen with 10 segments.

t: Which thoracic segment in cockroach does not bear wings?
s: The thorax of cockroach has prothorax, mesothorax and metathorax. Forewings (tegmina) arise from the mesothorax and hind wings from the metathorax, while the prothorax bears no wings; all three bear a pair of walking legs.

t: The skin of a frog is:
s: Frog skin is moist, smooth and slippery due to mucous glands, and highly vascular, allowing cutaneous respiration and water absorption. It lacks scales, hairs and a chitinous covering; dry scaly skin is reptilian, hair is mammalian and chitin is an arthropod feature.

t: In male frogs, the ureter functions as:
s: In male frog, sperms from the testes reach the kidney via vasa efferentia and Bidder's canal and then pass into the ureter. Thus the ureter carries both urine and sperms and functions as a urinogenital duct opening into the cloaca. In females the ureter carries urine only.

t: In frog which chamber pumps blood into the conus arteriosus?
s: In the frog heart, blood from the two atria enters the single ventricle, which contracts and pumps blood into the conus arteriosus, a sac-like structure on the ventral side opening from the ventricle. The sinus venosus joins the right atrium, and the atria pump into the ventricle, not the conus.

t: The forebrain of a frog consists of:
s: The frog brain has forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain. The forebrain includes the olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres and unpaired diencephalon. The midbrain has a pair of optic lobes, and the hindbrain consists of the cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
o: Cerebral hemisphere, olfactory lobes and diencephalon

t: Frog, Tadpole, Larva shows
s: The tadpole is an aquatic larva of the frog that breathes through gills, i.e. branchial respiration. Pulmonary (lung) and buccal respiration develop only after metamorphosis into the adult frog, which also uses cutaneous respiration.

t: The number of cranial nerves in frog is:
s: Frog has 10 pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain, as in fishes and other amphibians. Twelve pairs occur in reptiles, birds and mammals. Hence the correct number for frog is 10 pairs.

t: Renal portal system in frog connects:
s: In frog, the renal portal system is a special venous connection that brings blood from the lower parts of the body (hind limbs) to the kidneys before it returns to the heart. The hepatic portal system connects intestine and liver, and the hypophyseal portal connects hypothalamus and pituitary.
o: Kidney and lower parts of body
Kidney and upper parts of body

t: Adult frog excretes:
s: Adult frogs are ureotelic, excreting nitrogenous waste mainly as urea produced in the liver, which is eliminated through kidneys. Tadpoles are ammonotelic, while uric acid excretion (uricotelism) occurs in birds, reptiles and insects.

t: Muscles of stomach, intestine and blood vessels are:
s: The walls of internal organs like the stomach, intestine and blood vessels contain smooth muscle: fusiform cells without striations, whose contraction is involuntary and not under conscious control. Striated voluntary muscle is skeletal, and striated involuntary muscle is cardiac.

t: Which of the following is the characteristic feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism?

s: The tip of the nose is supported by cartilage, a specialised connective tissue with a solid, pliable matrix. Cartilage also forms the outer ear (pinna). Tendons are dense regular connective tissue, while the stomach and large intestine are mainly epithelium and smooth muscle.

t: Which of the following is known as tegmina in cockroach?

t: Lining of body cavities, ducts and tubes are made up of

t: Tissue that is most abundant and perform the functions of linking and supporting other tissues of the body are
s: Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed tissues in the body of complex animals. They link and support other tissues and organs. Epithelium covers and lines, muscle produces movement, and neural tissue controls responsiveness.

t: Fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells are present in
s: Areolar connective tissue, present beneath the skin, contains fibroblasts (secreting fibres), macrophages (phagocytic) and mast cells (secreting histamine, heparin) in a semi-fluid ground substance. t: Which of the following is common to bone and cartilage?
s: Both bone and cartilage are specialised connective tissues whose cells (osteocytes and chondrocytes) lie in small spaces called lacunae.
